title: Initial therapy for most adults with type 2 diabetes
condition: Type 2 diabetes requiring pharmacologic treatment without a clear insulin-first indication
recommendation: Lifestyle therapy plus metformin is a common initial pharmacologic approach when tolerated and not contraindicated.
notes: Use a patient-centered approach and reassess regularly if glycemic targets are not met.

title: Escalate beyond monotherapy when control remains above target
condition: Type 2 diabetes with HbA1c above individualized target or markedly elevated at presentation
recommendation: Consider early combination or add-on therapy rather than waiting for prolonged monotherapy failure.
notes: Escalation should reflect current treatment, glycemic burden, and patient-specific factors.

title: Consider insulin when hyperglycemia is severe
condition: Type 2 diabetes with catabolic features, symptomatic hyperglycemia, HbA1c greater than 10%, or blood glucose at or above 300 mg/dL
recommendation: Consider insulin initiation or insulin as the first injectable therapy.
notes: This is especially relevant when symptoms or ongoing catabolism suggest the patient needs faster glycemic control.

title: Prioritize cardiorenal benefit when comorbidities are present
condition: Type 2 diabetes with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, or heart failure
recommendation: Use an SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 receptor agonist with demonstrated cardiorenal benefit as part of the glucose-lowering regimen, independent of baseline HbA1c when appropriate.
notes: Comorbid cardiovascular, kidney, and heart failure status should influence agent selection early.

title: Continue metformin when intensifying therapy if tolerated
condition: Patient is already taking metformin and it remains tolerated without contraindication
recommendation: Continue metformin while adding another agent or insulin when additional glycemic control is needed.
notes: Metformin often remains part of combination therapy unless contraindications emerge.

title: Account for weight and hypoglycemia priorities
condition: Patient needs to minimize hypoglycemia or would benefit from weight reduction
recommendation: Prefer agents with lower hypoglycemia risk and consider weight-beneficial options such as GLP-1 receptor agonists or SGLT2 inhibitors when clinically appropriate.
notes: Treatment choice should reflect weight impact, hypoglycemia risk, cost, and patient preference.

title: Type 1 diabetes requires insulin therapy
recommendation: Insulin therapy is required; non-insulin medications are adjunctive only in selected situations.
notes: Adults with type 1 diabetes generally require insulin therapy for ongoing management.
